title: NY S07882: Prohibits a person or entity from knowingly or with reckless disregard facilitate an agreement between or among two or more residential rental property owners or managers to not compete with respect to residential rental dwelling units, including by operating or licensing a software, data analytics service, or algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function on behalf of or between and among such residential rental property owners or managers.

prohibitions: A person or entity must not knowingly or with reckless disregard facilitate an agreement between or among two or more residential rental property owners or managers to not compete with respect to residential rental dwelling units, including by operating or licensing a software, data analytics service, or algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function on behalf of or between and among such residential rental property owners or managers (Sec. 2)

A residential rental property owner or manager must not knowingly or with reckless disregard set or adjust rental prices, lease renewal terms, occupancy levels, or other lease terms and conditions in one or more of their residential rental properties based on recommendations from a software, data analytics service, or algorithmic device performing a coordinating function (Sec. 3)

Algorithmic device: any machine, device, computer program or computer software that on its own or with human assistance performs a coordinating function (Sec. 1(b))

What it does

This law makes it an unlawful violation for a person or entity to knowingly or with reckless disregard facilitate an agreement between or among two or more residential rental property owners or managers to not compete with respect to residential rental dwelling units, including by operating or licensing software, data analytics services, or algorithmic devices that perform a coordinating function. It also makes it an unlawful agreement for a residential rental property owner or manager to knowingly or with reckless disregard set or adjust rental prices, lease renewal terms, occupancy levels, or other lease terms and conditions based on recommendations from such a coordinating function.

Who it applies to

  • A person or entity who knowingly or with reckless disregard facilitates an agreement between or among two or more residential rental property owners or managers to not compete, including by operating or licensing a software, data analytics service, or algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function (Sec. 2)
  • A residential rental property owner or manager who knowingly or with reckless disregard sets or adjusts rental prices, lease renewal terms, occupancy levels, or other lease terms and conditions based on recommendations from a software, data analytics service, or algorithmic device performing a coordinating function (Sec. 3)

Effective date

the sixtieth day after it shall have become a law (Sec. 2 of the act)

Key definitions

  • Algorithm: a computational process that uses a set of rules to define a sequence of operations (Sec. 1(a))
  • Algorithmic device: any machine, device, computer program or computer software that on its own or with human assistance performs a coordinating function (Sec. 1(b))
  • Coordinating function: performing all of the following subfunctions, provided, however, that a product used for the purpose of establishing rent or income limits in accordance with the emergency tenant protection act of nineteen seventy-four, as amended, the rent stabilization law of nineteen sixty-nine, as amended, the city rent and rehabilitation law, the emergency housing rent control law, or an affordable housing program administered by a federal, state, or local government or other political subdivision shall not be considered to be performing a coordinating function: (i) collecting historical or contemporaneous prices, supply levels, or lease or rental contract termination and renewal dates of residential dwelling units from two or more residential rental property owners or managers, provided that at least two such residential rental property owners or managers are not wholly-owned subsidiaries of the same parent entity or otherwise owned or managed by the same residential rental property owner or manager; (ii) analyzing or processing the information described in subparagraph (i) of this paragraph using a system, software, or process that uses computation, including by using that information to train an algorithm; and (iii) recommending rental prices, lease renewal terms, ideal occupancy levels, or other lease terms and conditions to a residential rental property owner or manager (Sec. 1(c))
  • Residential rental property owner or manager: any individual or entity that owns or is a beneficial owner of, directly or indirectly, in whole or in part, or manages one or more residential rental dwelling units in New York state (Sec. 1(d))

Obligations

  • not stated in the text

Prohibitions

  • A person or entity must not knowingly or with reckless disregard facilitate an agreement between or among two or more residential rental property owners or managers to not compete with respect to residential rental dwelling units, including by operating or licensing a software, data analytics service, or algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function on behalf of or between and among such residential rental property owners or managers (Sec. 2)
  • A residential rental property owner or manager must not knowingly or with reckless disregard set or adjust rental prices, lease renewal terms, occupancy levels, or other lease terms and conditions in one or more of their residential rental properties based on recommendations from a software, data analytics service, or algorithmic device performing a coordinating function (Sec. 3)

Penalties and enforcement

The statute does not state who enforces it, what the penalties are, or whether there is a private right of action. It only declares certain conduct to be an unlawful violation or an unlawful agreement in violation of this article, and states that nothing in this section impairs or limits the applicability of any other part of this article or any other state law (Sec. 2, Sec. 3, Sec. 4).

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation that operates or licenses software, a data analytics service, or an algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function on behalf of or between and among residential rental property owners or managers may be in violation if it knowingly or with reckless disregard facilitates an agreement not to compete (Sec. 2)
  • A residential rental property owner or manager that uses such software, data analytics service, or algorithmic device to set or adjust rental prices, lease renewal terms, occupancy levels, or other lease terms and conditions based on its recommendations may be in violation (Sec. 3)
  • A product is only performing a coordinating function if it collects data from two or more residential rental property owners or managers who are not wholly-owned subsidiaries of the same parent entity or otherwise owned or managed by the same owner or manager, analyzes or processes that data computationally, and recommends rental prices, lease renewal terms, ideal occupancy levels, or other lease terms and conditions (Sec. 1(c))
  • A product used solely for establishing rent or income limits under specified rent control laws or an affordable housing program administered by a federal, state, or local government or other political subdivision is not considered to be performing a coordinating function (Sec. 1(c))

Notable exemptions

  • A product used for the purpose of establishing rent or income limits in accordance with the emergency tenant protection act of nineteen seventy-four, as amended, the rent stabilization law of nineteen sixty-nine, as amended, the city rent and rehabilitation law, the emergency housing rent control law, or an affordable housing program administered by a federal, state, or local government or other political subdivision shall not be considered to be performing a coordinating function (Sec. 1(c))

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether any software, data analytics service, or algorithmic device the organisation operates or licenses performs a coordinating function as defined in Sec. 1(c), including collecting data from two or more non-affiliated residential rental property owners or managers, analyzing or processing that data computationally, and recommending rental prices, lease renewal terms, ideal occupancy levels, or other lease terms and conditions (Sec. 1(c))
  • If the product performs a coordinating function, ensure it is not used to facilitate an agreement between or among two or more residential rental property owners or managers to not compete, and do not knowingly or with reckless disregard operate or license it for that purpose (Sec. 2)
  • If the organisation is a residential rental property owner or manager, do not knowingly or with reckless disregard set or adjust rental prices, lease renewal terms, occupancy levels, or other lease terms and conditions based on recommendations from such a coordinating function (Sec. 3)
  • Confirm whether the product is used solely for establishing rent or income limits under the specified rent control laws or affordable housing programs, which would mean it is not considered performing a coordinating function (Sec. 1(c))
